messages.subject: Instance Selection
parts:
Hi irace team,
My name is Somayeh, and I am a Ph.D. candidate at Shiraz University in Iran. Recently, I have decided to use the irace package for tuning the parameters of an algorithm which I have proposed to solve a routing problem. There are only 20 benchmark instances available for this problem that are hard to be solved due to their size. So, I used all of them as training instances. However, as you can see in the following figure, there is not any consistency in the values of rho, KenW, and Qvar in my experiments. In my view, this might stem from an unappropriated instance selection method. Would you please give me some advice regarding this issue?
I was also wondering if irace could determine the best value of a parameter in terms of a constant value. (e.g., the number of nodes in the graph associated with an instance)

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Instance Selection
parts:
Dear Somayeh,

You are right that the values of rho and KenW are a bit too low and the one of Qvar a bit too high, which indicates heterogeneous instances.  Please see the section on "Heterogeneous scenarios" in the user guide for some suggestions on how to handle such cases. Nevertheless, I would suggest to look at the values later in the execution, when more than 7 instances have been evaluated.

If you want that the parameter alpha depends on  the number of nodes "n" in the graph associated with an instance in parameter.txt, then define a dummy parameter in parameters.txt, for example:

alpha_factor "--alpha-factor " r (1,10)

Then, calculate alpha = alpha_factor * n or alpha = int(alpha_factor * n) if you want alpha to be an integer, within target-runner.

To get the value of "n", either:

1. Within target-runner, calculate "n" given the instance file.

2. Alternatively, define the instances in a file "train-instances.txt" such as:

instance-file-1.txt --n 12
instance-file-2.txt --n 15
instance-file-3.txt --n 19
...

and set

trainInstancesFile="train-instances.txt"

in scenario.txt. Now target-runner will receive an additional parameter "--n" with the value that corresponds to each instance. You'll need to handle that extra parameter.

The first approach is probably simpler in your case. The second approach is better when the instance feature takes long to compute (so it is better to precompute it and save its value in train-instances.txt) or it cannot be computed just from the instance data available in the input file.

I hope the above answers your questions.

Cheers,

Manuel.
